verses.text: Woe to the city of blood, full of lies, full of plunder, never without prey.

xrefs.text: Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town by iniquity!
Woe to the city of oppressors, rebellious and defiled!
Cursing and lying, murder and stealing, and adultery are rampant; one act of bloodshed follows another.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Woe to the city of bloodshed, to the pot now rusted, whose rust will not come off! Empty it piece by piece; cast no lots for its contents.
“As for you, son of man, will you judge her? Will you pass judgment on the city of bloodshed? Then confront her with all her abominations

verses.text: The crack of the whip, the rumble of the wheel, galloping horse and bounding chariot!

xrefs.text: at the sound of the galloping hooves of stallions, the rumbling of chariots, and the clatter of their wheels. The fathers will not turn back for their sons; their hands will hang limp.

The shields of his mighty men are red; the valiant warriors are dressed in scarlet. The fittings of the chariots flash like fire on the day they are prepared, and the spears of cypress have been brandished.
He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.
Then the hooves of horses thundered— the mad galloping of his stallions.
For every trampling boot of battle and every garment rolled in blood will be burned as fuel for the fire.

verses.text: Charging horseman, flashing sword, shining spear; heaps of slain, mounds of corpses, dead bodies without end— they stumble over their dead—

xrefs.text: Sun and moon stood still in their places at the flash of Your flying arrows, at the brightness of Your shining spear.
On the mountains of Israel you will fall— you and all your troops and the nations with you. I will give you as food to every kind of ravenous bird and wild beast.
Their slain will be left unburied, and the stench of their corpses will rise; the mountains will flow with their blood.
Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!
So He drove out the man and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.

verses.text: because of the many harlotries of the harlot, the seductive mistress of sorcery, who betrays nations by her prostitution and clans by her witchcraft.

xrefs.text: These two things will overtake you in a moment, in a single day: loss of children, and widowhood. They will come upon you in full measure, in spite of your many sorceries and the potency of your spells.
So take your stand with your spells and with your many sorceries, with which you have wearied yourself from your youth. Perhaps you will succeed; perhaps you will inspire terror!
Then one of the seven angels with the seven bowls came and said to me, “Come, I will show you the punishment of the great prostitute, who sits on many waters.
At the head of every street you built your lofty shrines and degraded your beauty. With increasing promiscuity, you spread your legs to all who passed by.
Then the kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her will weep and wail at the sight of the smoke rising from the fire that consumes her.

verses.text: “Behold, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.

xrefs.text: So I will pull your skirts up over your face, that your shame may be seen.
And if you ask yourself, “Why has this happened to me?” It is because of the magnitude of your iniquity that your skirts have been stripped off and your body has been exposed.
They will treat you with hatred, take all for which you have worked, and leave you naked and bare, so that the shame of your prostitution will be exposed. Your indecency and promiscuity

therefore I will surely gather all the lovers with whom you found pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from all around and expose you before them, and they will see you completely naked.
Take millstones and grind flour; remove your veil; strip off your skirt, bare your thigh, and wade through the streams.

verses.text: I will pelt you with filth and treat you with contempt; I will make a spectacle of you.

xrefs.text: “So I in turn have made you despised and humiliated before all the people, because you have not kept My ways, but have shown partiality in matters of the law.”
Babylon will become a heap of rubble, a haunt for jackals, an object of horror and scorn, without inhabitant.
My wounds are foul and festering because of my sinful folly.
then You would plunge me into the pit, and even my own clothes would despise me.
Sometimes you were publicly exposed to ridicule and persecution; at other times you were partners with those who were so treated.

verses.text: Then all who see you will recoil from you and say, ‘Nineveh is devastated; who will grieve for her?’ Where can I find comforters for you?”

xrefs.text: Who will have pity on you, O Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?
These pairs have befallen you: devastation and destruction, famine and sword. Who will grieve for you? Who can comfort you?
In fear of her torment, they will stand at a distance and cry out: “Woe, woe to the great city, the mighty city of Babylon! For in a single hour your judgment has come.

What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, O Daughter of Jerusalem? To what can I liken you, that I may console you, O Virgin Daughter of Zion? For your wound is as deep as the sea. Who can ever heal you?
“We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Abandon her! Let each of us go to his own land, for her judgment extends to the sky and reaches to the clouds.”

verses.text: Are you better than Thebes, stationed by the Nile with water around her, whose rampart was the sea, whose wall was the water?

xrefs.text: Cross over to Calneh and see; go from there to the great Hamath; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?
I will lay waste Pathros, set fire to Zoan, and execute judgment on Thebes.
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Behold, I am about to punish Amon god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh, Egypt with her gods and kings, and those who trust in Pharaoh.
“Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: ‘Who can be compared to your greatness?
The waters of the Nile will dry up, and the riverbed will be parched and empty.

verses.text: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were her allies.

xrefs.text: Cush, Put, and Lud, and all the various peoples, as well as Libya and the men of the covenant land, will fall with Egypt by the sword.
Men of Persia, Lydia, and Put served as warriors in your army. They hung their shields and helmets on your walls; they gave you splendor.
Those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast will be dismayed and ashamed.
The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

They cast lots for My people; they bartered a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine to drink.
On the day you stood aloof while strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gate and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were just like one of them.
Samaria will bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.

Arise, cry out in the night from the first watch of the night. Pour out your heart like water in the presence of the Lord. Lift up your hands to Him for the lives of your children who are fainting from hunger on the corner of every street.

verses.text: You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding and seek refuge from the enemy.

xrefs.text: Go into the rocks and hide in the dust from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty.

I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh; they will be drunk on their own blood, as with wine. Then all mankind will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”
Men will flee to caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, away from the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth.
Announce in Judah, proclaim in Jerusalem, and say: “Blow the ram’s horn throughout the land. Cry aloud and say, ‘Assemble yourselves and let us flee to the fortified cities.’

verses.text: All your fortresses are fig trees with the first ripe figs; when shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater!

xrefs.text: and the stars of the sky fell to the earth like unripe figs dropping from a tree shaken by a great wind.
They scoff at kings and make rulers an object of scorn. They laugh at every fortress and build up siege ramps to seize it.
The fading flower of his beautiful splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, will be like a ripe fig before the summer harvest: Whoever sees it will take it in his hand and swallow it.

verses.text: Look at your troops— they are like your women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire consumes their bars.

xrefs.text: The warriors of Babylon have stopped fighting; they sit in their strongholds. Their strength is exhausted; they have become like women. Babylon’s homes have been set ablaze, the bars of her gates are broken.
A sword is against her horses and chariots and against all the foreigners in her midst, and they will become like women. A sword is against her treasuries, and they will be plundered.
In that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble with fear beneath the uplifted hand of the LORD of Hosts, when He brandishes it against them.
The river gates are thrown open and the palace collapses.
This is what the LORD says to Cyrus His anointed, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him, to disarm kings, to open the doors before him, so that the gates will not be shut:

verses.text: Draw your water for the siege; strengthen your fortresses. Work the clay and tread the mortar; repair the brick kiln!

xrefs.text: One who scatters advances against you, O Nineveh. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Brace yourselves! Summon all your strength!
he consulted with his leaders and mighty men about stopping up the waters of the springs outside the city, and they helped him carry it out.
“Deploy your shields, small and large; advance for battle!
You saw that there were many breaches in the walls of the City of David. You collected water from the lower pool.
Advance, O horses! Race furiously, O chariots! Let the warriors come forth— Cush and Put carrying their shields, men of Lydia drawing the bow.

verses.text: There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you down and consume you like a young locust. Make yourself many like the young locust; make yourself many like the swarming locust!

xrefs.text: What the devouring locust has left, the swarming locust has eaten; what the swarming locust has left, the young locust has eaten; and what the young locust has left, the destroying locust has eaten.

“Behold, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will reduce your chariots to cinders, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voices of your messengers will no longer be heard.”
Look at your troops— they are like your women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire consumes their bars.
So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and throughout that day and night the LORD sent an east wind across the land. By morning the east wind had brought the locusts.
And He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria; He will make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as a desert.

verses.text: You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the sky. The young locust strips the land and flies away.

xrefs.text: You multiplied their descendants like the stars of heaven and brought them to the land You had told their fathers to enter and possess.
As the hosts of heaven cannot be counted and as the sand on the seashore cannot be measured, so too will I multiply the descendants of My servant David and the Levites who minister before Me.”
And the LORD took him outside and said, “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” Then He told him, “So shall your offspring be.”
I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the gates of their enemies.

verses.text: Your guards are like the swarming locust, and your scribes like clouds of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where.

xrefs.text: “Raise a banner in the land! Blow the ram’s horn among the nations! Prepare the nations against her. Summon the kingdoms against her— Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a captain against her; bring up horses like swarming locusts.
And the locusts looked like horses prepared for battle, with something like crowns of gold on their heads; and their faces were like the faces of men.

verses.text: O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber; your officers sleep. Your people are scattered on the mountains with no one to gather them.

xrefs.text: So Micaiah declared: “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, ‘These people have no master; let each one return home in peace.’”
The valiant lie plundered; they sleep their last sleep. No men of might could lift a hand.
Like a hunted gazelle, like a sheep without a shepherd, each will return to his own people, each will flee to his native land.
I will make her princes and wise men drunk, along with her governors, officials, and warriors. Then they will fall asleep forever and not wake up,” declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “I will punish the king of Babylon and his land as I punished the king of Assyria.

verses.text: There is no healing for your injury; your wound is severe. All who hear the news of you applaud your downfall, for who has not experienced your constant cruelty?

xrefs.text: For her wound is incurable; it has reached even Judah; it has approached the gate of my people, as far as Jerusalem itself.
All who pass by clap their hands at you in scorn. They hiss and shake their heads at the Daughter of Jerusalem: “Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?”
It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.
Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these countries and their lands.
Go up to Gilead for balm, O Virgin Daughter of Egypt! In vain you try many remedies, but for you there is no healing.
